newsitem.title: INDIA: Tribal militants kill 17 villagers in India.
newsitem.headline: Tribal militants kill 17 villagers in India.

text.p: Tribal guerrillas killed 17 people and wounded 20 in an attack on an Indian village, stepping up their fight for a separate nation in the remote northeast, authorities said on Wednesday.

Militants belonging to the All Tripura Tiger Force set fire to about 40 homes in Jarul Bachai in the western section of Tripura state late on Tuesday, then fired automatic weapons at fleeing residents, police in the state capital Agartala said.
Fifteen of the victims were killed on the spot while two died in hospital, a police officer in Calcutta said. Ten of the 20 wounded were in critical condition in hospital, he said.
Paramilitary forces were searching for the attackers, the police official said.

"The situation is volatile," Tripura Home (Interior) Minister Samar Chowdhury told Reuters by telephone. "We have already asked for more paramilitary forces from the centre (federal government) to tackle the situation."
Last July, the All Tripura Tiger Force issued a statement warning Bengali settlers to leave the state, which borders Bangladesh to the west.
The group's tribal insurgents, among dozens of militant groups in the northeast, have killed about 35 people in the past two months, authorities said.

The attack occurred near the Khowai region where on Sunday more than 60 houses were set on fire in ethnic clashes between tribals and Bengali settlers. The state government imposed a curfew on the Khowai region after Sunday's fighting.
On February 6, five people were killed in Khowai in ethnic clashes and police gunfire.
Tripura has an 840 kilometre (520 mile) border with Bangladesh.

The state's indigenous tribal population has been reduced to a minority by Bengali Hindus who began immigrating to the region before Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan, broke away after a nine-month war in 1971.
The immigrants now dominate local politics and the economy.

Chowdhury said local politicians were supporting the Bengali majority against militants, who he said were inflaming tribal resentment. "All these together are creating a riot-like situation," he said.
More than 2,000 people were killed in the region's worst ethnic riots in June 1980.
Chowdhury said the tension was currently restricted to the state's western district bordering Bangladesh and there had been no reports of violence in other areas.
"The security forces throughout the state have been alerted against possible militant attacks and subsequent ethnic clashes," Chowdhury said.
